documents.unit: Office of the Provost (AI Vision Committee)
documents.title: Policies and Principles on Using Generative AI Tools in Education
documents.summary: Committee proposal from July 2023 recommending university actions and sample syllabus statements for three approaches, plus assignment and assessment ideas and integrity-policy revisions. It sets no single rule itself and leaves the choice to instructors.
documents.stance_why: The proposal offers "No-AI", "Limited-AI" and "Full-AI" sample syllabus statements for instructors to pick from, and says Limited-AI use applies "when explicitly permitted by the instructor". It therefore sets no stance of its own and delegates to instructors, with tiers listed.

units.why: The introduction names the cheating worry as a "legitimate concern", framing why the committee writes policy; it is a rationale, not a rule, so informs/neutral. P56 (framework preamble) fits better than P36 because no misconduct rule is set.
units.anchor: legitimate concern that students will exploit GAI
units.resolution_why: A coded P56/all, B UNCOVERED/admin. The sentence ('there is a legitimate concern that students will exploit GAI for academic dishonesty or cheating') is a risk statement framing the proposal's purpose, which fits P56 (framework preamble); actor all, since it is not addressed to one group.

units.why: States that "students can leverage GAI to enhance their critical thinking skills" through discussion with AI content, a permissive rationale; P12 (AI as understanding aid) chosen over P44 because the point is learning, not career skill.
units.anchor: students can leverage GAI to enhance their critical thinking skills
units.resolution_why: A: student, permit; B: all, encourage. The passage says 'when used properly, students can leverage GAI to enhance their critical thinking', a conditional permission about student use, so student/permit; 'encourage' is stronger than the text.

units.why: Says GAI can serve in "the creation and debugging of computer programs", a statement that AI help with coding and debugging is valuable; P13 fits debugging help, as a rationale (informs).
units.anchor: creation and debugging of computer programs
units.resolution_why: A: unit_stance permit; B: encourage. 'GAI can also serve as a valuable tool ... in the creation and debugging of computer programs' states a possible use, not a recommendation, so permit.

units.why: States GAI "can aid in improving writing abilities by providing suggestions, grammar corrections, and even generating draft content", naming permissible prose uses, so P18 (prose separate from code).
units.anchor: GAI can aid in improving writing abilities by providing suggestions, grammar corrections
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. The sentence 'GAI can aid in improving writing abilities by providing suggestions, grammar corrections' is a real statement of a permitted use (prose support, P18); kept.

units.why: Calls for "a balance between leveraging AI tools for support and preserving the authenticity and originality of student work"; a principle for the whole framework, hence P56 rather than P32.
units.anchor: balance between leveraging AI tools for support and preserving the authenticity
units.resolution_why: Both coded P56 and informs. A: all, B: admin. 'It is crucial to maintain a balance' is a principle for the whole community, so actor all.

units.why: States the committee objective to "harness the potential of GAI as a valuable educational resource while safeguarding the principles of academic integrity", a purpose statement for the framework, so P56.
units.anchor: harness the potential of GAI as a valuable educational resource
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. 'A key objective of the AI Vision Committee is to ... harness the potential of GAI ... while safeguarding the principles of academic integrity' states the purpose and principle of the framework (P56); kept.

units.why: Raises "concerns regarding bias and fairness in AI-generated content" and harms to democracy; names ethical harms, so P53.
units.anchor: concerns regarding bias and fairness in AI-generated content
units.resolution_why: Both P53. B's anchor covers the whole bias and equity sentence; A split equity into its own unit, so bias is matched and equity is kept as an A-only unit.

units.why: Names "equity issues surrounding how different types of students can access such tools", an access concern; P51 covers equity and access though no remedy is given, so informs.
units.anchor: equity issues surrounding how different types of students can access such tools
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B folded it into its bias unit). The text names 'equity issues surrounding how different types of students can access such tools' separately from bias, so it is kept as its own P51 unit.

units.why: States Fordham "has an opportunity to help students develop AI literacy" so they use tools "ethically and responsibly"; AI literacy as a skill, P44.
units.anchor: help students develop AI literacy

units.why: Frames Jesuit values ("Cura Personalis", RomeCall) as the basis to "prioritize AI ethics, social justice inclusivity, and individual well-being", an institution-level principle, so P56.
units.anchor: Fordham can prioritize AI ethics, social justice inclusivity, and individual well-being
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. 'Fordham can prioritize AI ethics, social justice inclusivity, and individual well-being' states a guiding principle (P56); kept.

units.why: Says "it is essential to educate students to use GAI responsibly and ethically", an education commitment about responsible use, so P44.
units.anchor: it is essential to educate students to use GAI responsibly and ethically
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. 'it is essential to educate students to use GAI responsibly and ethically' is a distinct statement from the literacy opportunity sentence; kept as P44 encourage.

units.why: Immediate action asks the administration to "review and update the integrity statement", a revision of the policy in light of AI; P54 (revisit policy) rather than P36 since no misconduct rule is stated here.
units.anchor: review and update the integrity statement

units.why: Recommends deans send "a statement regarding the responsible use of generative AI tools" to faculty; an institution-level framework communication (P56), not a syllabus requirement (P09).
units.anchor: disseminate a statement regarding the responsible use of generative

units.why: Asks chairs to "revisit their learning goals in light of rapid advances in GAI"; redesign of courses around AI (P35).
units.anchor: revisit their learning goals in light of rapid advances in GAI

units.why: Recommends "workshops on GAI literacy for faculty members"; supporting faculty in learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: workshops on GAI literacy for faculty members

units.why: Recommends "a dedicated point of contact for faculty members" for technology and teaching questions; faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: dedicated point of contact for faculty members

units.why: Declares the university "committed to promoting critical AI literacy among students, faculty, and staff"; teaching AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: committed to promoting critical AI literacy among students, faculty, and staff
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. 'Fordham University is committed to promoting critical AI literacy among students, faculty, and staff' is a stated institutional commitment about AI in teaching; kept.

units.why: Recommends "technical support and guidance to students, faculty, and staff on the effective utilization of GAI" via tutorials and workshops; effective-use skill (P44).
units.anchor: effective utilization of GAI

units.why: The recommendation says the revised integrity statements 'will provide frameworks for students to identify the use of GAI in completing the course work'. It is addressed to the university (it asks for frameworks to be built), is institutional set-up, and concerns disclosure of AI use, so P24 with should.
units.anchor: frameworks for students to identify the use of GAI in completing the course work
units.resolution_why: Both coded P24, student, should. Phase differed: A during-work, B over-time. The sentence describes what updated university integrity statements will contain, so the binding actor is the university (admin) and the phase is institutional set-up (before-course). Type P24 (disclosure) kept by both.

units.why: Same passage covers faculty identifying GAI use "in research and other scholarly publications" and involving the IRB; research governance, P62.
units.anchor: faculty to identify the use of GAI in research
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B's anchor spanned both the student and the faculty clause). 'for faculty to identify the use of GAI in research and other scholarly publications' is a separate disclosure rule for faculty in research (P62); kept.

units.why: Says faculty identify GAI use "in research and other scholarly publications" and recommends involving "the IRB and University Research Council", governing AI in research, so P62.
units.anchor: involving the IRB and University Research Council to ensure the responsible
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. 'involving the IRB and University Research Council to ensure the responsible and ethical use of GAI in research' is a distinct recommendation on research governance (P62); kept.

units.why: Recommends "a dedicated forum" where faculty share teaching strategies and tools; faculty learning community, P63.
units.anchor: dedicated forum, such as a center, consortium

units.why: Recommends an FAQ page covering how to maintain integrity and cite AI; supports faculty and students in understanding AI (P63 nearest; P09 not fitting since it is not a syllabus rule).
units.anchor: Create a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) page
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. B treated the FAQ list as questions only. Creating the FAQ page is the recommendation, so the unit is kept as P63; the sample questions themselves are not policy.

units.why: Offers sample syllabus statements in three named approaches ("No-AI", "Limited-AI", "Full-AI"); named tiers, P05.
units.anchor: the committee offers the following statements for inclusion in course syllabi
units.resolution_why: A: may, course-start; B: informs, before-course. The committee 'offers the following statements for inclusion in course syllabi', an offer addressed to instructors for use when stating expectations, so may and course-start.

units.why: The No-AI template says "Generative AI tools are not permitted in this course", a course-wide ban; P01.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are not permitted in this course.

units.why: The No-AI template says students 'must rely on their own originality, creativity and critical thinking skills to complete assignments'. It requires the student's own thinking to do the work, so P32 (primary problem-solver); P29 (ownership of what is submitted) concerns submissions, which this sentence does not mention. It follows the ban just stated, so prohibit.
units.anchor: must rely on their own originality, creativity and critical thinking skills
units.resolution_why: A: P29; B: P32. The sentence is about relying on the student's own thinking to complete assignments, not about owning a submission, so P32.

units.why: Limited-AI template: usage "may be allowed for specific assignments... when explicitly permitted by the instructor", so AI is allowed assignment by assignment; P04 (instructor/assignment decides) rather than P02.
units.anchor: may be allowed for specific assignments in this course
units.resolution_why: A: during-work; B: course-start. It is part of the Limited-AI syllabus template, which communicates expectations, so course-start. Both coded P04 and restrict.

units.why: Limited-AI: "mandatory to clearly indicate the sections of your work that were generated" by AI; disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: mandatory to clearly indicate the sections of your work that were generated

units.why: Limited-AI: students must "indicate the prompts and software versions that were used"; specific citation details, P25.
units.anchor: indicate the prompts and software versions that were used

units.why: Limited-AI: "refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content" is an ethical-standards duty; plagiarism is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content
units.resolution_why: A: P36, unit_stance neutral; B: UNCOVERED, restrict. Plagiarism and misleading content by AI users is improper AI use treated as misconduct, which fits P36; because it limits how AI may be used, unit_stance is restrict.

units.why: Limited-AI: "Additional guidelines or restrictions will be provided for specific assignments", so assignment-level rules; P04.
units.anchor: Additional guidelines or restrictions will be provided for specific assignments.

units.why: Full-AI template: "This course allows the use of generative AI tools"; default permission with encouragement of exploration, P02.
units.anchor: This course allows the use of generative AI tools
units.resolution_why: A: during-work; B: course-start. The Full-AI sentence is a syllabus template, so course-start.

units.why: Full-AI template: students "must clearly indicate the sections of the work that were generated" with AI; P24.
units.anchor: Students must clearly indicate the sections of the work

units.why: Full-AI template also requires indicating "the prompts and software versions that were used"; P25.
units.anchor: prompts and software versions that were used

units.why: The Full-AI template also says 'It is critical to adhere to ethical standards by refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content'. Improper AI use is treated as misconduct, so P36; it limits permitted use, so restrict.
units.anchor: refraining from activities like plagiarism or creating misleading content
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (A coded the sentence only in the Limited-AI template). The Full-AI template repeats the sentence in a separate template that instructors may choose, so it is kept, with the same type as its Limited-AI counterpart (P36, not UNCOVERED).

units.why: Suggested assignment where students "revise and edit AI-generated texts" and "submit both the original AI draft and their final version", an AI-based assignment design with drafts, so P35.
units.anchor: Students will submit both the original AI draft and their final version.
units.resolution_why: A: P26, student, should, require; B: P35, instructor, may, encourage. The sentence ends a suggested assignment ('Assign students to revise and edit AI-generated texts ... Students will submit both the original AI draft and their final version'), offered to instructors. P26 would fit the submission rule alone, but the passage is an assignment design idea, so P35 with instructor and may.

units.why: Suggests AI-embracing assignments such as "in-class discussions analyzing AI-generated writing"; assignments redesigned around AI, P35.
units.anchor: in-class discussions analyzing AI-generated writing
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. 'Conduct in-class discussions analyzing AI-generated writing' is a suggested assignment for instructors who embrace GAI; kept, phase during-work like its sibling bullets.

units.why: Suggests "in-class presentations comparing and contrasting AI writing with human writing", an AI-embracing assignment, so P35.
units.anchor: Organize in-class presentations comparing and contrasting AI writing with human writing.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. 'Organize in-class presentations comparing and contrasting AI writing with human writing' is one of the suggested GAI assignments; kept.

units.why: Suggests students "compose variations of the same prompt to fine-tune AI-generated results", an assignment teaching prompt use, so P35.
units.anchor: having students compose variations of the same prompt to fine-tune AI-generated results
units.resolution_why: Found only by B. 'having students compose variations of the same prompt to fine-tune AI-generated results' is one of the suggested GAI assignments; kept.

units.why: Among suggested assignments for instructors, the text says 'encouraging students to interact with AI, using it for brainstorming or divergent thinking exercises'. It is an idea offered to instructors, so actor instructor and may, and it allows AI for brainstorming (P15).
units.anchor: using it for brainstorming or divergent thinking exercises
units.resolution_why: A: student, should; B: instructor, should. Both coded P15 and encourage. The bullet is an idea offered to instructors in a list of 'some suggested ideas', so actor instructor and may.

units.why: Deterrent idea: "Require oral presentation of coursework" to assess understanding; P34.
units.anchor: Require oral presentation of coursework to assess students' understanding

units.why: Deterrent idea: "interactive, in-class exercises" for real-time application; moves work to in-class, P33.
units.anchor: interactive, in-class exercises to promote active learning

units.why: Case studies on current events are "a short-term defense" against AI; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Engage in case studies based on current events.
units.resolution_why: A: before-course; B: during-work. Case studies are assignments students complete, listed among the sample assignments, so during-work.

units.why: For AI-prohibited assignments, "Assess the uniqueness of content using plagiarism detection tools"; similarity checking, P40.
units.anchor: Assess the uniqueness of content using plagiarism detection tools

units.why: Warns existing tools "are highly imperfect" and may misflag non-native writers; detector unreliability, P39.
units.anchor: existing tools are highly imperfect

units.why: Suggests comparing "take-home assignments with in-class work" to spot AI; comparative evidence of misuse, P40.
units.anchor: Compare the quality and creativity of take-home assignments with in-class work

units.why: Suggests having students "reflect on GAI's benefits and limitations" in AI-allowed assignments; reflections, P26.
units.anchor: reflect on GAI's benefits and limitations, justifying their responses
units.resolution_why: A: neutral; B: encourage. The bullet asks students to reflect on AI's benefits and limitations as an assessment idea; it takes no position on using AI, so neutral.

units.why: Suggests requiring students to "submit the prompts used for GAI" and assessing adaptation of output; prompt logs, P26.
units.anchor: Require students to submit the prompts used for GAI
units.resolution_why: A: neutral; B: encourage. Same reasoning as the reflection bullet: submitting prompts is an assessment idea, not a stance on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: Appendix rubric "helps educators review assignment prompts for vulnerabilities to generative AI tools"; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: review assignment prompts for vulnerabilities to generative AI tools

units.why: Recommends faculty be "encouraged to incorporate a dedicated section in their course syllabi" on generative AI; syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: explicit statement on the acceptable use of generative AI in the syllabus

units.why: Faculty should "reconsider the role and format of assignments" with AI tools; P35.
units.anchor: reconsider the role and format of assignments
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B's anchor spanned this and the next sentence). 'faculty members should reconsider the role and format of assignments' is a separate recommendation to redesign assignments (P35); kept.

units.why: Says assessments should "be designed to reduce the temptation of cheating"; redesign around AI, P35.
units.anchor: assessments can be designed to reduce the temptation of cheating

units.why: Asks program leaders to consider "preparing students for post-graduation studies and careers in a world with these tools"; career rationale, P44.
units.anchor: preparing students for post-graduation studies and careers in a world

units.why: Asks area chairs to "review and update program learning goals" for AI; program-level redesign, P35.
units.anchor: review and update program learning goals
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Section 3c asks area chairs and program directors to 'review and update program learning goals', a separate recommendation from the immediate action on department chairs; kept.

units.why: Writing Center should "lead campus discussions on the responsible integration" of AI incl. plagiarism awareness and training; support and training, P63.
units.anchor: lead campus discussions on the responsible integration of generative AI tools

units.why: The Academic Integrity Statement "will be carefully reviewed and updated" to address generative AI; policy revision, P54 (not P36, as it sets no misconduct rule itself).
units.anchor: Statement and Standards will be carefully reviewed and updated
units.resolution_why: A: must; B: informs. The sentence says the standards 'will be carefully reviewed and updated', a commitment to revise, so must.

units.why: Deans 'will inform all students' of the revised standards with 'clear guidelines and expectations regarding the use of generative AI tools'. It sets up the university-wide framework and communicates it to students, so P56 fits and UNCOVERED is not needed.
units.anchor: Deans will inform all students
units.resolution_why: A: UNCOVERED; B: P56. The passage communicates the university-wide integrity framework to students; P56 (institution-wide framework) fits closely enough, so the uncovered label is dropped.

units.why: Recommends "active collaboration with industry leaders" to learn "the expected AI literacy of graduates"; career-relevant AI skill, P44.
units.anchor: expected AI literacy of graduates
units.resolution_why: A: should, over-time; B: informs, general. The committee 'recommends active collaboration with industry leaders' to learn the expected AI literacy of graduates, a recommendation, so should.

documents.title: Fordham Policy on AI
documents.summary: Landing page for the Fordham Policy on AI. It describes how the Provost created the AI Vision Committee and links the committee proposal; it states no rules itself.
documents.stance_why: The page only says the committee was established "to substantively assess the policies" and links to the proposal; it states no AI-use rule and defers to the linked recommendations, so it delegates.

units.why: The page says the Provost established the AI Vision Committee "to substantively assess the policies, strategies and safeguards" for GAI in teaching and research; an institutional framework statement, P56.
units.anchor: to substantively assess the policies, strategies and safeguards

documents.title: Standards of Academic Integrity
documents.summary: University Standards of Academic Integrity. Work must be done without external help including AI tools unless the instructor authorizes it, and AI misuse is listed under plagiarism and falsification. Instructors are urged to put this and a GAI policy in syllabi.
documents.stance_why: Students must complete work "without assistance from external resources (including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools) unless directly authorized by the instructor", so AI is banned unless permitted; this is restrict.

units.why: Students must work "without assistance from external resources (including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools)"; AI is barred as the default for all assignments, P01.
units.anchor: without assistance from external resources (including any artificial intelligence or machine-learning tools)

units.why: The exception "unless directly authorized by the instructor" puts the permission decision with the instructor; P04 rather than P06 since no silent-syllabus case is described.
units.anchor: unless directly authorized by the instructor

units.why: Violators face "sanctions ranging from a reduction in grade, course failure in the assignment, or expulsion"; stated penalties, P37.
units.anchor: sanctions ranging from a reduction in grade, course failure in the assignment, or expulsion

units.why: "It is strongly recommended that instructors place the above paragraph in their syllabi" (which bars AI unless authorized); syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: strongly recommended that instructors place the above paragraph in their syllabi
units.resolution_why: A: course-start; B: before-course. The sentence asks instructors to put the paragraph in syllabi, i.e. to communicate expectations, so course-start.

units.why: "GAI policies should be included as well" using the AI Vision Committee language; a syllabus AI statement (P09).
units.anchor: GAI policies should be included as well
units.resolution_why: A: course-start; B: before-course. Same reasoning: syllabus statements communicate expectations, so course-start.

units.why: Plagiarism includes work prepared by "generative artificial intelligence when not expressly permitted"; AI misuse classed as plagiarism, P36 (P19 not chosen since the point is the misconduct label).
units.anchor: or generative artificial intelligence when not expressly permitted
units.resolution_why: A: actor all; B: student. The plagiarism standard applies to what students present as their own work, so student.

units.why: Falsification includes "the usage of artificial intelligence to complete an assignment claimed to be one's own"; forbids AI-produced submitted work, P19 (P36 considered, but the rule is about submitting AI work as own).
units.anchor: the usage of artificial intelligence to complete an assignment claimed to be one's own
units.resolution_why: A: P19; B: P36. The falsification item bans 'the usage of artificial intelligence to complete an assignment claimed to be one's own', which is the rule about AI-made submitted work, so P19. The plagiarism item above is coded P36 because it only classifies the misconduct.

notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Dropped as non-policy or out of scope: FAQ sample questions (B), the statement that integrity revisions will clarify consequences (duplicate of the revision unit), internal research funding and community workshops (scholarship and external engagement, not AI use in teaching and learning), and the standards' generic citation duty (no AI mention). Course layer deferred in collection; no school or computing-unit policy found.
